title: On‑Prem Handoff Gaps + Action Compact (weekly)
content:
Meeting: Private Deploys — Handoff & Field Gaps (weekly compact)
Date: 2026-07-15
Facilitator: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Aisha, Connor, María, Ethan, SRE on-call (Sam), Solutions (Priya)
Objective: Triage customer-facing install gaps discovered last week, align on short tactical fixes, and agree on next steps for runbook/automation to avoid repeat work.

Summary / Observations:
- Pattern: 3 installs this sprint hit the same class of preflight/network/environment issues rather than product regressions. Good sign: runtime is stable when env is correct. Bad sign: we lack a short, automatable preflight that matches common customer infra.
- Telemetry gap: installs often pass, but post-handoff we see missing agent heartbeats for the first 24h because node labeling and serviceAccount permissions differ across air-gapped customers.
- Security integration friction: HSM/KMS handshakes failed on two installs because customer-side HSM supports only RSA-PSS and our client library attempted RSA-PKCS1-v1_5 by default.

Notable customer-specific blockers (short notes):
1) Acme Logistics (DEPLOY-3892) — Network / MTU mismatch & BGP path issues
   - Symptom: large-model pulls stall; subsequent container restarts due to OOM-like behavior when large chunks retransmit.
   - Root cause hypothesis: MTU on host network set to 1400, jumbo frames expected by our data-plane for gRPC chunking. BGP next-hop filtering caused asymmetric return path.
   - Temporary mitigation applied: set service mesh to use chunk-size=8k and enabled TCP MSS clamping on install node. Customer network team investigating permanent MTU change.

2) MediSystems (DEPLOY-3927) — HSM handshake fails during key-import
   - Symptom: install halts at kms-init step with "unsupported padding/cipher" error.
   - Root cause: vendor HSM only supports RSA-PSS. Our KMS client lib defaults to PKCS1.
   - Action taken: provided a patched client and instructions to enable compatibility mode on the HSM. Long-term: add KMS client auto-detect and fallback.

3) FinGuard (internal ticket DEPLOY-3945) — Air-gapped signing mismatch and package verification
   - Symptom: packages fail verification because downstream signing metadata uses SHA-256 while their verifier expects SHA-512.
   - Note: this is customer policy; we delivered a shim that re-signs artifacts with configured algo. Proposal: ship a signing-compat helper in the air-gap bundle.

Operational / telemetry notes:
- Missing logs: several sites did not run the post-install telemetry-agent due to a systemd unit name mismatch after package upgrade (unit: redwood-telemetry vs redwood-telemetry-agent).
- Observability impact: dashboards show delayed model-load metrics; SRE asks for a heartbeat metric within 10 minutes of first container ready.
- Quick win: add a small init-check in the installer that validates the systemd unit presence and uses journalctl to fetch the last 500 lines for triage uploads.

Short-term tactical actions (this week):
- A1 (owner: Connor Li) — Ship a 1.1.3 preflight script (single-file bash + python fallback) that checks: MTU >= 1400, outbound NAT exists for registry access, firewall rules for TCP 443/4443 and 10250 open, DNS resolution for our package registry. Due: 2026-07-17.
- A2 (owner: María González) — Patch KMS client to try RSA-PSS and PKCS1 fallbacks; add feature-flagged auto-detect. Create a binary artifact and test against MediSystems' HSM emulator. Due: 2026-07-20.
- A3 (owner: Ethan Park) — Create an "air-gap signing helper" to include in the air-gap tarball. Minimal UX: re-sign artifacts for customer's configured algo. Due: 2026-07-21.
- A4 (owner: SRE Sam) — Add installer hook to verify telemetry unit name and upload initial logs to support bundle automatically. Due: 2026-07-18.
- A5 (owner: Priya / Solutions) — Draft customer-facing "network preflight checklist" (one pager) that we run in kickoff calls. Include MTU, BGP asymmetry checks, proxy/NAT expectations. Due: 2026-07-16.

Medium-term engineering improvements (next 2–8 weeks):
- Preflight automation: convert the single-file script into a lightweight Go binary that returns structured JSON with machine-readable errors and suggested fixes (priority: high).
- KMS compatibility matrix: publish a matrix of HSM vendors, supported ciphers/paddings, and known workarounds. Link from install runbook.
- Installer telemetry: create heartbeat metric emitted by installer; wire into Console onboarding page so support sees first-30m health immediately.
- Helm chart validation: add stricter schema checks for nodeSelectors/taints that commonly cause scheduling failures in on-prem clusters.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should we make the MTU > 1400 requirement explicit in docs or try to remove the dependency by changing chunking behavior globally? Pros/cons discussed: explicit requirement reduces surprises but increases hand-holding; runtime change adds complexity and risk.
- For air-gapped installs, do we require a minimal signing policy or ship helper shims? Immediate customer momentum prefers helper shims.

Escalations requested:
- Solutions to contact Acme network lead to drive MTU change; if no change in 5 business days we will schedule an on-site (or shared remote packet capture session) with field eng. (Owner: Aisha)
- Security: need approval for shipping KMS client fallback behavior flagged as "compatibility" (owner: María) — security review request raised (linked artifact).

Notes to self / informal follow-ups:
- Keep the preflight script tiny and idempotent; support teams should be able to run it in <90s on a cold host and paste output into ticket.
- Capture a small example of journalctl + systemctl output to show the unit-name mismatch in the runbook PR.

Decisions made:
- Ship preflight script as immediate stop-gap (Connor).
- Build KMS fallback as feature-flagged change behind security review (María).
- Air-gap bundle will include signing helper v0.1 (Ethan).

Next meeting: 2026-07-22 10:00 PT — quick sync on progress and any escalations.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting commands (to paste in tickets)
- Check MTU: ip link show dev <iface> | grep mtu
- Test outbound egress: curl -v --connect-timeout 5 https://packages.redwood.ai/health || echo "egress-fail"
- Journal snippet: sudo journalctl -u redwood-telemetry -n 200 --no-pager
- KMS handshake debug: REDWOOD_KMS_DEBUG=1 ./kms-client --test-import \"path/to/pkcs8\"

End of compact notes.
